title: Chapter 253: A Hammer to the Face
html:
“Help!”

It was midnight in the countryside, and no other vehicles traveled the road. Remembering the final message on his phone, Uncle Zhang avoided the woods and fled down the center of the pavement. Wind roared in his ears. After several meters, he realized he could hear no footsteps behind him and looked back.

“You can’t escape!” The face on the back of the passenger’s head had become grotesquely distorted, as though trying to crawl free. The man was only half a meter behind Uncle Zhang.

It wants to drill into my head.

Uncle Zhang did not know why that certainty entered his mind, but he focused on escape. He dared not look back again. Yet refusing to see something did not make it disappear.

A needling pain pierced the back of his skull, like the point of a knife pressing slowly inward.

“Help!” he screamed, but silence alone answered. Cold spread across his neck, and he lacked even the strength to look back. His pace faltered as his lungs emptied. He could run no farther.

“You’ll get used to it.” The eerie voice sounded directly behind his head. Uncle Zhang forced himself onward. Woods lined both sides of the road, which led only to the crematorium; almost no one traveled it at night.

His skull felt as though it were being peeled open. The agony was unbearable. Uncle Zhang’s eyes rolled upward, and consciousness began slipping away.

“So painful!”

That was the only thought in his mind. That and… Will I become a monster with a face on the back of my head when I wake up?

Cold invaded his mind, muddling his memories. Reaching his limit, Uncle Zhang collapsed. Something icy slithered along his back like a venomous snake, and he was powerless to stop it. The pain in his skull intensified. He tried to scream but had lost his voice. Shaking his head did nothing to dislodge the thing.

“So painful…”

His lips had not moved, yet a voice entered his ear. “Was that me?”

With his consciousness fraying, Uncle Zhang turned toward the sound. Headlights were the darkness’s only illumination. Trees rustled beside the road as something approached.

“So painful, so painful!”

The voice continued, and Uncle Zhang’s face turned ashen when he realized it did not come from him.

Another monster is coming?

Uncle Zhang struggled to keep his eyes open. All he had wanted was to earn a living for his family. He had never imagined it would end like this.

Will someone operate on my body to investigate after I die?

Strange thoughts drifted through his mind. The cold on his back began to recede, though the pain in his skull remained. The passenger also sensed danger in that voice and quickened his movements.

How come the monster feels like it is afraid?

Before his eyes closed, Uncle Zhang saw a taxi approaching. He tried to warn its occupants, but his lips would not move. The door flew open, and the lunatic he had encountered twice emerged carrying a backpack.

Why is he here?

The lunatic dropped the bag, pulled out a terrifying hammer, and charged straight toward Uncle Zhang.

I’m definitely going to die this time.

Despair swallowed Uncle Zhang, and precious memories flashed through his mind. Two meters away, the man raised the hammer and aimed directly at the back of his head.

BANG!

The pain vanished instantly. A human-shaped figure tumbled backward and rolled across the road. Bone cracked loudly, and red flooded Uncle Zhang’s vision. With great difficulty, he turned his head. The sight of his passenger’s mangled body overwhelmed the last of his composure, and terror dragged him fully unconscious.

“Don’t be afraid!” Chen Ge gasped, having arrived just in time. Uncle Zhang was already unconscious and heard nothing. The second driver climbed from his car and screamed at the sight.

“Uncle Zhang! Wake up!” The cries shattered the night’s silence. Upon seeing Chen Ge, the passenger scrambled to his feet and fled into the woods.

“Call the police immediately! Tell them the culprit is an escaped patient from the Third Sick Hall!”

After issuing the order, Chen Ge pursued the man into the forest. Tangled undergrowth slowed both hunter and prey.

After several minutes, the passenger began to weaken. He staggered from side to side, one shoulder shattered by the earlier blow, every stride threatening to tear his body apart.

“You’re not going to run away!”

Chen Ge would not let him escape. Whether for the hidden mission or the safety of others, he intended to consign the Ghost Stories Society to history. Hearing Chen Ge’s taunt, the passenger gritted his teeth. Only minutes earlier, he had spoken the same words to Uncle Zhang.

The passenger caught his foot on a root, and his unbalanced body crashed to the ground.

“Finished running?” Chen Ge seized the opportunity and closed the distance, the hammer swelling in the passenger’s terrified vision.

Panic seized the passenger. He crawled deeper into the forest, but Chen Ge found him within seconds. The hammer swept toward his leg. At the last instant, the man dug in an elbow and wrenched his body aside.

BANG!

The hammer struck a tree trunk, shaking the entire tree. The passenger’s face went whiter than a corpse.

“Don’t force me!” The face on the back of his head stirred. Blood vessels seeped through its skin and wove themselves into a new shape. Within seconds, it had transformed into an eerie likeness of Chen Ge.

“You’re definitely from behind the door if you can control these blood vessels.”

Before the transformation finished, Chen Ge charged. Against monsters from behind the door, he would never hold back.

“I’ve been waiting for you!”

As Chen Ge approached, the passenger sprang up and grappled him with all his remaining strength. The imitation face smiled sickly and leaned toward Chen Ge’s own.

He had devised this plan the moment he saw Chen Ge, but overlooked one crucial detail. In the narrow space between the two identical faces, a bloodcurdling scream erupted.

“Painful... so painful!”
